options.A: The underlying reason why the deviation or failure occurred (e.g. lack of control or training)
options.B: The police station where the crime was reported
options.C: The total amount of tax collected

correctAnswerText: The underlying reason why the deviation or failure occurred (e.g. lack of control or training)
explanation: Cause explains why the discrepancy arose, enabling constructive audit recommendations for systemic rectification.

questionText: The 'Effect' element of an audit finding illustrates:

options.A: The financial loss, risk, inefficiency, or negative impact resulting from the deviation
options.B: The weather on the day of audit
options.C: The date the report is published
options.D: The name of the audit assistant

correctAnswerText: The financial loss, risk, inefficiency, or negative impact resulting from the deviation
explanation: Effect quantifies the monetary damage, waste, or loss of public benefit caused by the violation of criteria.

questionText: An Exit Conference (or Exit Meeting) is held at the conclusion of field audit to:

options.A: Discuss initial audit observations with the head of the auditee entity and record their viewpoints
options.C: Celebrate the conclusion of the fiscal year
options.D: Collect personal gifts from the management

correctAnswerText: Discuss initial audit observations with the head of the auditee entity and record their viewpoints
explanation: The Exit Conference provides a transparent forum for the audit team and management to review draft observations and factual accuracy.

questionText: Quality Assurance and Quality Control in the Department of the Auditor General of Pakistan is guided by:

options.A: ISSAI 140 (Quality Control for SAIs)

correctAnswerText: ISSAI 140 (Quality Control for SAIs)
explanation: ISSAI 140 sets forth the standards for quality control systems in Supreme Audit Institutions.

questionText: Can the Auditor General of Pakistan audit private companies having no state ownership or government funding?

options.A: No, the AGP's constitutional mandate extends to public accounts, state enterprises, and authorities receiving public funds
options.B: Yes, the AGP can audit any private family business without restriction
options.C: Yes, upon payment of a commercial fee
options.D: Only if the company manufactures food

correctAnswerText: No, the AGP's constitutional mandate extends to public accounts, state enterprises, and authorities receiving public funds
explanation: The AGP's mandate is strictly defined by Articles 168-171 of the Constitution to state organs, public enterprises, and government authorities.

questionText: The fundamental value of Supreme Audit Institutions is described in ISSAI 12 as:

options.A: Making a difference to the lives of citizens by strengthening public accountability and transparency

correctAnswerText: Making a difference to the lives of citizens by strengthening public accountability and transparency
explanation: ISSAI 12 defines the value and benefits of SAIs: making a difference to the lives of citizens through enhanced governance and public accountability.

questionText: Which Article of the Constitution of the Islamic Republic of Pakistan, 1973 provides for the appointment of the Auditor General of Pakistan?

options.A: Article 168

correctAnswerText: Article 168
explanation: Article 168(1) states: 'There shall be an Auditor-General of Pakistan, who shall be appointed by the President.'

questionText: Who appoints the Auditor General of Pakistan under Article 168(1)?

options.A: The Prime Minister
options.C: The Chairman of the Public Accounts Committee

correctAnswerText: The President of Pakistan
explanation: Under Article 168(1), the Auditor-General of Pakistan is appointed by the President.

questionText: Before entering upon office, the Auditor General makes an oath before the:

options.A: President of Pakistan

correctAnswerText: Chief Justice of Pakistan
explanation: Article 168(2) specifies that before entering upon office, the Auditor-General shall make before the Chief Justice of Pakistan an oath in the form set out in the Third Schedule.

questionText: What is the fixed constitutional term of office of the Auditor General of Pakistan under Article 168(3)?

options.A: 3 years

correctAnswerText: 4 years
explanation: Under Article 168(3) (as amended by 18th Amendment), the Auditor-General holds office for a single term of 4 years.

questionText: Is the Auditor General of Pakistan eligible for re-appointment or extension in term after completing four years?

options.A: Yes, for another term of 4 years
options.B: Yes, with approval of the Prime Minister
options.C: No, the Auditor-General shall not be eligible for further appointment in that office

correctAnswerText: No, the Auditor-General shall not be eligible for further appointment in that office
explanation: Article 168(3) expressly stipulates: '...and shall not be eligible for further appointment in that office.'

questionText: Can the Auditor General of Pakistan be removed from office before the expiry of their term?

options.A: Yes, by an executive order of the Prime Minister
options.B: Yes, on the same ground and in the same manner as a Judge of the Supreme Court (Article 209)
options.D: Yes, by a simple majority vote in the Senate

correctAnswerText: Yes, on the same ground and in the same manner as a Judge of the Supreme Court (Article 209)
explanation: Article 168(5) provides that the Auditor-General shall not be removed from office except in the like manner and on the like grounds as a Judge of the Supreme Court (via Supreme Judicial Council under Article 209).

questionText: Which constitutional body inquires into the capacity or misconduct of the Auditor General for removal purposes?

options.A: The Federal Public Service Commission
options.B: The Supreme Judicial Council under Article 209

correctAnswerText: The Supreme Judicial Council under Article 209
explanation: Because the AGP enjoys equivalent protection to a Supreme Court Judge, inquiries for removal are conducted by the Supreme Judicial Council under Article 209.

questionText: Under Article 168(4), can a person who has held office as Auditor General hold any office of profit in the service of Pakistan?

options.A: Yes, in any ministry
options.B: No, except that they may be appointed as an Ambassador or Federal Minister
options.C: No, they shall not be eligible for further appointment in the service of Pakistan before the expiration of two years after ceasing to hold that office
options.D: Yes, immediately upon retirement without bar

correctAnswerText: No, they shall not be eligible for further appointment in the service of Pakistan before the expiration of two years after ceasing to hold that office
explanation: Article 168(4) bars appointment in the service of Pakistan until the expiration of two years after demitting office.

questionText: The terms and conditions of service of the Auditor General are determined by:

options.A: Act of Majlis-e-Shoora (Parliament)

correctAnswerText: Act of Majlis-e-Shoora (Parliament)
explanation: Article 168(3) provides that the terms and conditions of service of the Auditor-General shall be determined by Act of Majlis-e-Shoora (Parliament).

questionText: Pending an Act of Parliament, the terms and conditions of service of the AGP are governed by:

options.A: Auditor-General's (Functions, Powers and Terms and Conditions of Service) Ordinance, 2001 (Ordinance XXIII of 2001)

correctAnswerText: Auditor-General's (Functions, Powers and Terms and Conditions of Service) Ordinance, 2001 (Ordinance XXIII of 2001)
explanation: Ordinance XXIII of 2001 was promulgated under the constitutional authority to regulate AGP functions, powers, and service conditions.

questionText: Under Article 168(6), who performs the functions of Auditor General when the office is vacant or the AGP is absent?

options.A: The senior-most officer of the Inter-Services Intelligence
options.B: Such other person as the President may direct to act as Auditor-General
options.C: The Controller General of Accounts automatically
options.D: The Secretary of the Ministry of Finance

correctAnswerText: Such other person as the President may direct to act as Auditor-General
explanation: Article 168(6) states the President may appoint an Acting Auditor-General during vacancy or absence.

questionText: Article 169 of the Constitution of Pakistan defines the:

options.A: Appointment of Supreme Court judges
options.B: Functions and powers of the Auditor General of Pakistan

correctAnswerText: Functions and powers of the Auditor General of Pakistan
explanation: Article 169 is titled 'Functions and powers of Auditor-General' relating to the accounts of the Federation, Provinces, and statutory authorities.

questionText: Under Article 169, the Auditor General performs functions relating to the accounts of:

options.A: Only the Federal Government
options.B: The Federation and of the Provinces and of any authority or body established by the Federation or a Province

correctAnswerText: The Federation and of the Provinces and of any authority or body established by the Federation or a Province
explanation: The AGP's constitutional remit encompasses the Federation, all four Provinces, and all statutory authorities/bodies created by federal or provincial law.

questionText: Article 170(1) of the Constitution empowers the Auditor General to:

options.A: Direct the form and principles according to which the accounts of the Federation and Provinces shall be kept, with the approval of the President

correctAnswerText: Direct the form and principles according to which the accounts of the Federation and Provinces shall be kept, with the approval of the President
explanation: Article 170(1) states: 'The accounts of the Federation and of the Provinces shall be kept in such form and in accordance with such principles and methods as may be specified by the Auditor-General with the approval of the President.'

questionText: Article 170(2), inserted by the 18th Constitutional Amendment, expressly authorizes the AGP to:

options.A: Audit the accounts of all authorities and bodies established by or under the control of the Federal or Provincial Governments
options.B: Command the military forces during peace
options.D: Regulate the State Bank interest rates

correctAnswerText: Audit the accounts of all authorities and bodies established by or under the control of the Federal or Provincial Governments
explanation: Article 170(2) empowers the AGP to conduct the audit of accounts of any authority, corporation, or body established by or under the control of the Federal or a Provincial Government.

questionText: Article 171 of the Constitution governs the:

options.A: Salary of members of Parliament
options.B: Reports of the Auditor General of Pakistan

correctAnswerText: Reports of the Auditor General of Pakistan
explanation: Article 171 is titled 'Reports of Auditor-General'.

questionText: To whom does the Auditor General submit the reports relating to the accounts of the Federation under Article 171?

options.A: The Prime Minister

correctAnswerText: The President of Pakistan
explanation: Article 171 specifies that reports relating to the accounts of the Federation shall be submitted to the President.

questionText: What does the President do upon receiving the Auditor General's report under Article 171?

options.A: Keeps it in executive secrecy
options.B: Causes the report to be laid before both Houses of Majlis-e-Shoora (Parliament)
options.C: Submits it to the Supreme Court for approval
options.D: Sends it directly to the Federal Board of Revenue

correctAnswerText: Causes the report to be laid before both Houses of Majlis-e-Shoora (Parliament)
explanation: Article 171 mandates: '...who shall cause them to be laid before both Houses of Majlis-e-Shoora (Parliament).'

questionText: To whom does the Auditor General submit the reports relating to the accounts of a Province under Article 171?

options.A: The Chief Minister
options.C: The Speaker of the Provincial Assembly directly

correctAnswerText: The Governor of the Province
explanation: Article 171 provides that reports relating to the accounts of a Province shall be submitted to the Governor of that Province.

questionText: The Governor of a Province causes the Auditor General's provincial report to be laid before:

options.A: The Provincial Assembly

correctAnswerText: The Provincial Assembly
explanation: Article 171 requires the Governor to cause the provincial audit reports to be laid before the Provincial Assembly.

questionText: The retirement age of the Auditor General of Pakistan under Ordinance XXIII of 2001 is:

options.A: 60 years
options.D: No age limit provided the 4-year term is not exceeded

correctAnswerText: 65 years
explanation: Under Section 4 of Ordinance XXIII of 2001, the AGP shall retire on completing 4 years in office or attaining the age of 65 years, whichever occurs earlier.

questionText: The salary, pension, and allowances of the Auditor General of Pakistan are:

options.A: Voted annually by Parliament in the budget
options.B: Charged expenditure upon the Federal Consolidated Fund under Article 81
options.C: Determined by commercial profit of the DAGP

correctAnswerText: Charged expenditure upon the Federal Consolidated Fund under Article 81
explanation: Under Article 81(b) of the Constitution, the administrative expenses of the office of the Auditor-General, including remuneration, are 'Charged' upon the Federal Consolidated Fund, ensuring financial independence.

questionText: What does 'Charged Expenditure' upon the Federal Consolidated Fund mean?

options.A: It can be discussed in the National Assembly but is NOT submitted to the vote of the Assembly
options.B: It cannot be discussed at all
options.C: It must be approved by provincial assemblies
options.D: It is paid through external foreign loans

correctAnswerText: It can be discussed in the National Assembly but is NOT submitted to the vote of the Assembly
explanation: Under Article 82(1), charged expenditures can be discussed in Parliament but cannot be voted upon or reduced by the National Assembly.

questionText: Under Ordinance XXIII of 2001, the Auditor General has the power to:

options.A: Inspect any office of accounts under the control of Federation or Province
options.B: Require the production of any books, accounts, contracts, stores, or other documents
options.C: Ask such information and explanations as may be necessary for discharging audit duties

correctAnswerText: All of the above
explanation: Section 12 of Ordinance XXIII of 2001 grants the AGP comprehensive powers of inspection, requisition of records, and calling for information.

questionText: If an auditee department refuses to produce records demanded by an audit team of the AGP, it constitutes:

options.A: An acceptable administrative privilege
options.B: Obstruction in performance of constitutional duty and a serious breach of law
options.C: An ordinary administrative delay without consequence
options.D: A matter solely for the interior ministry

correctAnswerText: Obstruction in performance of constitutional duty and a serious breach of law
explanation: Denial of access violates Article 169/170 and Section 12 of Ordinance XXIII of 2001 and is reported as a serious scope limitation.

questionText: Can the Federal or Provincial Governments restrict the scope of audit conducted by the Auditor General?

options.A: Yes, through an executive summary
options.B: No, the Auditor General's constitutional scope cannot be curtailed by executive fiat
options.D: Yes, with permission of the Deputy Commissioner

correctAnswerText: No, the Auditor General's constitutional scope cannot be curtailed by executive fiat
explanation: The AGP's constitutional mandate under Articles 168-171 cannot be abridged or impeded by administrative executive orders.

questionText: The administrative expenses of the Office of the Auditor General are charged under which Article of the Constitution?

options.A: Article 81(b)

correctAnswerText: Article 81(b)
explanation: Article 81(b) specifically lists the administrative expenses of the office of the Auditor-General as Charged on the Federal Consolidated Fund.

questionText: Which Schedule of the Constitution of 1973 contains the official Oath of Office of the Auditor General?

options.A: First Schedule

correctAnswerText: Third Schedule
explanation: The form of oath of office for the Auditor-General is prescribed in the Third Schedule of the 1973 Constitution.

questionText: Under Section 8 of Ordinance XXIII of 2001, the Auditor General has the authority to audit:

options.A: All receipts which are payable into the Federal Consolidated Fund or Public Account
options.B: All expenditure from the Federal Consolidated Fund or Public Account
options.C: Accounts of stores and stocks kept in any office or department of Federation/Province

correctAnswerText: All of the above
explanation: Section 8, 9, and 10 of the Ordinance give the AGP full mandate over receipts, expenditures, stores, and stocks of the Federation and Provinces.

questionText: Can the Auditor General of Pakistan delegate their powers to subordinate audit officers?

options.A: No, all powers must be exercised personally
options.B: Yes, under Section 16 of Ordinance XXIII of 2001, powers may be delegated to officers subordinate to the AGP

correctAnswerText: Yes, under Section 16 of Ordinance XXIII of 2001, powers may be delegated to officers subordinate to the AGP
explanation: Section 16 authorizes the AGP to delegate powers to subordinate officers of the Department of the Auditor General of Pakistan.

questionText: The Department of the Auditor General of Pakistan (DAGP) is an institution that belongs to which branch of the state?

options.A: Executive branch completely
options.B: An independent Supreme Audit Institution (SAI) established by the Constitution to support legislative oversight
options.C: Subordinate department of State Bank of Pakistan

correctAnswerText: An independent Supreme Audit Institution (SAI) established by the Constitution to support legislative oversight
explanation: The SAI of Pakistan is a constitutional watchdog external to the executive, assisting the legislature in enforcing executive accountability.

questionText: Which constitutional amendment introduced Article 170(2) to explicitly expand the AGP's audit mandate over state-controlled bodies?

options.A: 17th Amendment

correctAnswerText: 18th Amendment (2010)
explanation: The 18th Constitutional Amendment (2010) inserted Clause (2) into Article 170, clarifying the AGP's authority over all public bodies and authorities.

questionText: Prior to the 18th Amendment, the tenure of the Auditor General under Ordinance XXIII of 2001 was 5 years. What did the 18th Amendment fix it to?

options.A: 3 years

correctAnswerText: 4 years non-extendable
explanation: The 18th Amendment amended Article 168(3) to constitutionalize a fixed 4-year non-extendable term.

questionText: Under the Constitution, does the Auditor General have the judicial power to convict or imprison corrupt individuals directly?

options.A: Yes, the AGP has summary trial powers
options.B: No, the AGP reports audit findings and financial irregularities to Parliament, which holds the executive accountable
options.C: Yes, the AGP acts as High Court judge

correctAnswerText: No, the AGP reports audit findings and financial irregularities to Parliament, which holds the executive accountable
explanation: The AGP is an auditor and reporting authority, not a court; enforcement and prosecution belong to PAC, NAB, FIA, or the courts.

questionText: The office of the Auditor General of Pakistan was historically separated from the accounting function in:
correctAnswerText: 2001 (via Ordinances XX and XXIII)
explanation: In 2001, the Department of AGP was departmentalized, separating Accounts (Controller General of Accounts - CGA) from independent Audit (AGP).

questionText: Which ordinance established the Controller General of Accounts (CGA) in 2001?

options.A: Ordinance XXIV of 2001

correctAnswerText: Ordinance XXIV of 2001
explanation: Ordinance XXIV of 2001 established the CGA to oversee government accounting, while Ordinance XXIII of 2001 governed the AGP.

questionText: Under Article 168(5), a reference for the removal of the Auditor General can be initiated through:

options.A: The President directing the Supreme Judicial Council to conduct an inquiry

correctAnswerText: The President directing the Supreme Judicial Council to conduct an inquiry
explanation: Like a Supreme Court Judge under Article 209, the President directs the Supreme Judicial Council to investigate allegations of misconduct or physical/mental incapacity.

questionText: Under Article 170, whose prior approval is required when the Auditor General specifies the principles and methods of keeping accounts?

options.A: The Prime Minister

correctAnswerText: The President
explanation: Article 170(1) states: '...as may be specified by the Auditor-General with the approval of the President.'

questionText: Are public defense expenditures subject to audit by the Auditor General of Pakistan?

options.A: No, defense is completely exempt
options.B: Yes, Defense Services accounts are audited by the Directorate General Audit (Defense Services) under the AGP

correctAnswerText: Yes, Defense Services accounts are audited by the Directorate General Audit (Defense Services) under the AGP
explanation: Under Article 169, all public expenditure from the Federal Consolidated Fund, including Defense, falls within the AGP's audit jurisdiction.

questionText: The Auditor General of Pakistan submits reports on public commercial enterprises under:

options.A: Directorate General Commercial Audit and Evaluation

correctAnswerText: Directorate General Commercial Audit and Evaluation
explanation: The DG Commercial Audit & Evaluation carries out audit of commercial state-owned entities (SOEs) on behalf of the AGP.

questionText: Can the Provincial Public Accounts Committee summon the Federal Auditor General directly?

options.A: No, the AGP is represented by the respective Provincial Director General of Audit in provincial PACs
options.B: Yes, the AGP must attend all 4 provincial PACs personally every day
options.C: No, provincial accounts are audited by private accountants

correctAnswerText: No, the AGP is represented by the respective Provincial Director General of Audit in provincial PACs
explanation: The AGP delegates representation in provincial assemblies to the relevant Provincial Director General of Audit (e.g. DG Audit Punjab/Sindh/KP/Balochistan).

questionText: The constitutional independence of the AGP is reinforced by which of the following provisions?

options.A: Security of tenure equivalent to a Supreme Court Judge
options.B: Expenses charged on the Federal Consolidated Fund
options.C: Bar on re-employment in government for 2 years after demitting office

correctAnswerText: All of the above
explanation: Tenure security, charged expenditures, and bars on executive patronage all ensure the AGP's independence from political and executive pressure.

questionText: Under Ordinance XXIII of 2001, who appoints the officers and staff of the Department of the Auditor General?

options.A: The Auditor General of Pakistan in accordance with prescribed rules
options.C: The Federal Public Service Commission alone

correctAnswerText: The Auditor General of Pakistan in accordance with prescribed rules
explanation: Section 15 of Ordinance XXIII of 2001 authorizes the AGP to appoint officers and staff in accordance with rules.

questionText: Audit of 'Trading, Manufacturing and Profit and Loss Accounts' of government departments is authorized under:

options.A: Section 9 of Ordinance XXIII of 2001

correctAnswerText: Section 9 of Ordinance XXIII of 2001
explanation: Section 9 mandates the AGP to audit trading, manufacturing, profit and loss accounts and balance sheets kept in any government department.

questionText: The term of office of an Acting Auditor General appointed under Article 168(6) continues until:

options.A: A permanent Auditor General enters upon the office

correctAnswerText: A permanent Auditor General enters upon the office
explanation: The acting appointment terminates as soon as a regular Auditor-General is appointed and makes oath under Article 168(2).

questionText: Does the Auditor General have the power to examine the accounts of local governments (District/City Governments)?

options.A: Yes, under local government statutes and provincial audit commands
options.B: No, local governments are exempt from any audit
options.C: Only if requested by foreign donors

correctAnswerText: Yes, under local government statutes and provincial audit commands
explanation: Local government accounts are audited by dedicated Local Government Audit Directorates within the DAGP framework.

questionText: The Auditor General's Annual Report on the accounts of the Federation typically includes:

options.A: Audit Report on Federal Government Accounts (Civil)
options.C: Audit Report on Public Sector Enterprises and Commercial Undertakings

correctAnswerText: All of the above
explanation: The AGP presents specialized volumes covering Federal Civil, Defense, Commercial Undertakings, Revenue Receipts, and Water & Power.

questionText: Can the National Assembly or Senate alter the constitutional provisions governing the AGP through an ordinary executive notification?

options.A: Yes, by a simple administrative letter
options.B: No, constitutional amendments require a two-thirds majority in both Houses of Parliament under Article 239

correctAnswerText: No, constitutional amendments require a two-thirds majority in both Houses of Parliament under Article 239
explanation: Articles 168 to 171 are entrenched constitutional provisions that cannot be amended without a two-thirds constitutional amendment.

questionText: Which Article of the Constitution gives the definition of the 'Federal Consolidated Fund' audited by the AGP?

options.A: Article 78

correctAnswerText: Article 78
explanation: Article 78(1) defines the Federal Consolidated Fund, comprising all revenues received, loans raised, and loan repayments to the Federal Government.

questionText: The Auditor General of Pakistan is an active member of which international regional supreme audit body?

options.A: ASOSAI (Asian Organization of Supreme Audit Institutions)
options.C: INTOSAI (International Organization of Supreme Audit Institutions)

correctAnswerText: All of the above
explanation: The AGP is a key member of INTOSAI, ASOSAI, and ECOSAI (and has previously hosted the ECOSAI headquarters).

questionText: Audit Planning in the Department of the Auditor General of Pakistan begins with:

options.A: Strategic Audit Planning and entity risk profiling
options.D: Inviting public tenders for audit tools

correctAnswerText: Strategic Audit Planning and entity risk profiling
explanation: The audit process commences with Strategic Audit Planning, where auditee entities are mapped and classified according to financial and operational risk.
subCategory: Audit Planning, Conduct, Reporting & PAC Role

questionText: An Operational Audit Plan prepared by a field audit directorate details:

options.A: Resource allocation, audit execution schedules, team compositions, and target auditee formations
options.B: The political manifesto of the government
options.C: The personal leave records of drivers
options.D: The daily lunch menu of the audit team

correctAnswerText: Resource allocation, audit execution schedules, team compositions, and target auditee formations
explanation: The Operational Audit Plan translates strategic priorities into tangible quarterly/annual audit execution schedules with budgeted man-days.
subCategory: Audit Planning, Conduct, Reporting & PAC Role

questionText: Audit Execution phase consists of:

options.A: Entry conference, field testing/verification, issuing audit memos, and exit conference
options.B: Writing the final book directly without fieldwork

correctAnswerText: Entry conference, field testing/verification, issuing audit memos, and exit conference
explanation: Execution encompasses opening discussions (entry meeting), sampling, substantive testing, recording observations, and concluding exit meetings.
subCategory: Audit Planning, Conduct, Reporting & PAC Role

questionText: An 'Entry Conference' at the start of field audit serves to:

options.A: Introduce the audit team, discuss audit scope, objectives, and establish liaison protocols with management
options.C: Lock the premises of the entity

correctAnswerText: Introduce the audit team, discuss audit scope, objectives, and establish liaison protocols with management
explanation: The Entry Conference builds professional rapport, explains audit objectives, and outlines required documentation.
subCategory: Audit Planning, Conduct, Reporting & PAC Role

questionText: What is an 'Audit Memorandum' (or Audit Query)?

options.A: A formal written observation issued by the field audit team to the entity management seeking clarification or documentation on observed anomalies
options.D: A dismissal order for an employee

correctAnswerText: A formal written observation issued by the field audit team to the entity management seeking clarification or documentation on observed anomalies
explanation: Audit memos are issued during fieldwork to give auditees immediate opportunity to provide explanations or missing records.
subCategory: Audit Planning, Conduct, Reporting & PAC Role

questionText: If an auditee furnishes satisfactory documentary evidence resolving an audit memo during fieldwork, the audit team:

options.A: Drops the observation and records the justification in working papers
options.B: Converts it into a draft para anyway

correctAnswerText: Drops the observation and records the justification in working papers
explanation: If credible, verifiable evidence satisfies the criteria, the observation is settled and dropped at the field level.
subCategory: Audit Planning, Conduct, Reporting & PAC Role

questionText: The forum established at the Ministry/Division level to settle unresolved audit observations is the:

options.A: Departmental Accounts Committee (DAC)

correctAnswerText: Departmental Accounts Committee (DAC)
explanation: The DAC is the departmental oversight body tasked with reviewing audit observations and settling compliant queries prior to PAC submission.
subCategory: Audit Planning, Conduct, Reporting & PAC Role

questionText: Who chairs the Departmental Accounts Committee (DAC)?

options.A: The Secretary of the Ministry/Division (Principal Accounting Officer - PAO)

correctAnswerText: The Secretary of the Ministry/Division (Principal Accounting Officer - PAO)
explanation: The Secretary of the administrative ministry, in their capacity as Principal Accounting Officer (PAO), presides over the DAC.
subCategory: Audit Planning, Conduct, Reporting & PAC Role

questionText: The Public Accounts Committee (PAC) of Pakistan is a standing committee of the:

options.A: National Assembly of Pakistan

correctAnswerText: National Assembly of Pakistan
explanation: Under the Rules of Procedure and Conduct of Business in the National Assembly, the PAC is a parliamentary standing committee.
subCategory: Audit Planning, Conduct, Reporting & PAC Role

questionText: The primary constitutional role of the Public Accounts Committee is to:

options.A: Examine whether public funds appropriated by Parliament have been spent legally, economically, and for the intended purposes as reported by the AGP
options.B: Prepare the national budget for the upcoming fiscal year

correctAnswerText: Examine whether public funds appropriated by Parliament have been spent legally, economically, and for the intended purposes as reported by the AGP
explanation: PAC scrutinizes appropriation accounts, finance accounts, and the Auditor General's audit reports to ensure executive accountability to Parliament.
subCategory: Audit Planning, Conduct, Reporting & PAC Role

questionText: Who assists the Public Accounts Committee as an independent expert advisor during its examination of audit reports?

options.A: The Auditor General of Pakistan and their senior officers

correctAnswerText: The Auditor General of Pakistan and their senior officers
explanation: The AGP acts as the primary professional and technical guide to the PAC, presenting audit findings and verifying departmental compliance.
subCategory: Audit Planning, Conduct, Reporting & PAC Role

questionText: The Principal Accounting Officer (PAO) appearing before the Public Accounts Committee to defend ministry accounts is the:

options.A: Secretary of the concerned Ministry or Division

correctAnswerText: Secretary of the concerned Ministry or Division
explanation: The Federal Secretary (or head of department) is the PAO personally accountable before the PAC for financial stewardship of the ministry.
subCategory: Audit Planning, Conduct, Reporting & PAC Role

questionText: Under the Rules of Procedure of the National Assembly, the Public Accounts Committee has the power to:

options.A: Summon persons, call for papers, records, and administer oaths to witnesses

correctAnswerText: Summon persons, call for papers, records, and administer oaths to witnesses
explanation: The PAC enjoys powers analogous to a civil court to enforce attendance, examine witnesses on oath, and compel production of state records.
subCategory: Audit Planning, Conduct, Reporting & PAC Role

questionText: When the PAC examines an Appropriation Account, it satisfies itself that:

options.A: The moneys shown in the accounts as having been disbursed were legally available for and applicable to the service or purpose
options.B: The expenditure conforms to the authority which governs it
options.C: Every re-appropriation has been made in accordance with prescribed rules

correctAnswerText: All of the above
explanation: National Assembly Rule 201 mandates PAC to examine legality, authority, compliance, and validity of re-appropriations.
subCategory: Audit Planning, Conduct, Reporting & PAC Role

questionText: An 'Excess Grant' occurs when:

options.A: Actual expenditure incurred by a ministry exceeds the amount voted and appropriated by Parliament for that grant
options.B: A ministry saves 50% of its budget

correctAnswerText: Actual expenditure incurred by a ministry exceeds the amount voted and appropriated by Parliament for that grant
explanation: Excess expenditure beyond parliamentary grant requires post-facto regularization by the National Assembly upon PAC recommendation.
subCategory: Audit Planning, Conduct, Reporting & PAC Role

questionText: How is an Excess Grant regularized under the Constitution of Pakistan?

options.A: The National Assembly votes on an Excess Demand for Grant after PAC examination
options.B: The Prime Minister signs a private waiver
options.C: The Auditor General forgives the excess
options.D: The Supreme Court issues a stay order

correctAnswerText: The National Assembly votes on an Excess Demand for Grant after PAC examination
explanation: Article 84 of the Constitution requires excess expenditure to be laid before the National Assembly as a Supplementary/Excess Demand for Grant.
subCategory: Audit Planning, Conduct, Reporting & PAC Role

questionText: The decisions, recommendations, and orders issued by the Public Accounts Committee are termed:

options.A: PAC Directives

correctAnswerText: PAC Directives
explanation: PAC formal recommendations are known as 'PAC Directives', which executive ministries are bound to implement.
subCategory: Audit Planning, Conduct, Reporting & PAC Role

questionText: The implementation and follow-up of PAC Directives is monitored by the:

options.A: PAC Monitoring & Implementation (M&I) Cell / PAC Secretariat and DAGP

correctAnswerText: PAC Monitoring & Implementation (M&I) Cell / PAC Secretariat and DAGP
explanation: A specialized Monitoring & Implementation wing within the National Assembly Secretariat and DAGP tracks compliance with PAC directives.
subCategory: Audit Planning, Conduct, Reporting & PAC Role

questionText: If the PAC uncovers severe financial fraud or criminal embezzlement during its hearings, it may direct the matter to be investigated by:

options.A: National Accountability Bureau (NAB) or Federal Investigation Agency (FIA)

correctAnswerText: National Accountability Bureau (NAB) or Federal Investigation Agency (FIA)
explanation: PAC routinely refers evidence of criminal malfeasance to investigative agencies like NAB or FIA for criminal prosecution.
subCategory: Audit Planning, Conduct, Reporting & PAC Role

questionText: Can the Public Accounts Committee examine expenditures incurred by the Defense Services?

options.A: Yes, through the Sub-Committee or In-Camera sessions reviewing DG Audit Defense reports
options.B: No, defense is strictly barred from parliamentary scrutiny
options.C: Only if requested by foreign ambassadors

correctAnswerText: Yes, through the Sub-Committee or In-Camera sessions reviewing DG Audit Defense reports
explanation: Defense accounts are examined by PAC, frequently in in-camera proceedings to address sensitive national security dimensions.
subCategory: Audit Planning, Conduct, Reporting & PAC Role

questionText: An Audit Para included in the AGP's formal report to Parliament is classified into categories based on severity, such as:

options.A: Draft Paras, Commercial Audit Observations, and Special Study Paras

correctAnswerText: Draft Paras, Commercial Audit Observations, and Special Study Paras
explanation: Audit paras are categorized by materiality, nature of irregularity (fraud, recovery, overpayment, system failure), and type of audit.
subCategory: Audit Planning, Conduct, Reporting & PAC Role

questionText: What is an 'Advance Para'?

options.A: An audit observation sent by the Audit Directorate to the PAO for departmental consideration and reply within a prescribed timeframe (usually 6 weeks)
options.B: A cash loan granted to civil servants
options.C: A clause in the military manual

correctAnswerText: An audit observation sent by the Audit Directorate to the PAO for departmental consideration and reply within a prescribed timeframe (usually 6 weeks)
explanation: Advance paras are written notices sent to PAOs before compiling the final Audit Report, allowing ministries to respond.
subCategory: Audit Planning, Conduct, Reporting & PAC Role

questionText: If the PAO fails to respond to an Advance Para within the stipulated time, what happens?

options.A: The observation is incorporated as a Draft Para in the printed Auditor General's Report to Parliament
options.B: The audit team forgets the issue
options.C: The money is written off automatically

correctAnswerText: The observation is incorporated as a Draft Para in the printed Auditor General's Report to Parliament
explanation: Failure of departmental response or unsatisfactory reply causes the observation to be printed in the annual report laid before Parliament.
subCategory: Audit Planning, Conduct, Reporting & PAC Role

questionText: What is the primary role of the Auditor General during PAC meetings?

options.A: Presenting the facts of the audit para, assessing departmental replies, and advising PAC whether compliance is verified
options.D: Arresting corrupt witnesses in the room

correctAnswerText: Presenting the facts of the audit para, assessing departmental replies, and advising PAC whether compliance is verified
explanation: The AGP acts as the expert advisor, confirming whether recovered funds have been verified and whether corrective action satisfies audit rules.
subCategory: Audit Planning, Conduct, Reporting & PAC Role

questionText: Can the Public Accounts Committee write off government financial losses on its own authority?

options.A: No, PAC recommends actions to the National Assembly and directs ministries to seek proper executive write-off sanction or recovery under rules
options.B: Yes, PAC can forgive all national debt
options.C: Yes, by oral proclamation of the Chairman
options.D: PAC can only double the loss

correctAnswerText: No, PAC recommends actions to the National Assembly and directs ministries to seek proper executive write-off sanction or recovery under rules
explanation: PAC directs recovery or regularisation; formal write-offs must follow financial procedures and sanctions from the Finance Division.
subCategory: Audit Planning, Conduct, Reporting & PAC Role

questionText: A 'Recovery Para' in an audit report refers to an observation where:

options.A: Public funds were overpaid, unauthorizedly disbursed, or misappropriated and must be recovered into the treasury
options.D: A tax rebate was granted legally

correctAnswerText: Public funds were overpaid, unauthorizedly disbursed, or misappropriated and must be recovered into the treasury
explanation: Recovery paras involve identifiable monetary losses, overpayments, or illegal allowances that must be deposited back into government revenues.
subCategory: Audit Planning, Conduct, Reporting & PAC Role

questionText: The Public Accounts Committee typically consists of how many members in the National Assembly of Pakistan?

options.A: Approximately 20 to 30 members representing both government and opposition parties

correctAnswerText: Approximately 20 to 30 members representing both government and opposition parties
explanation: The PAC comprises approximately 25-30 Members of National Assembly (and includes Senators in joint PAC setups) reflecting proportional party representation.
subCategory: Audit Planning, Conduct, Reporting & PAC Role

questionText: The democratic convention often followed in the National Assembly of Pakistan regarding the PAC Chairmanship is that:

options.A: The Leader of the Opposition or an Opposition member is appointed Chairman PAC to ensure independent oversight
options.B: The Minister of Finance is always Chairman
options.C: The Prime Minister serves as Chairman

correctAnswerText: The Leader of the Opposition or an Opposition member is appointed Chairman PAC to ensure independent oversight
explanation: Under democratic parliamentary convention (Charter of Democracy), the PAC chairmanship is traditionally offered to the opposition to prevent self-auditing.
subCategory: Audit Planning, Conduct, Reporting & PAC Role

questionText: In provincial assemblies of Pakistan, who scrutinizes the Auditor General's Provincial Audit Reports?

options.A: The Provincial Public Accounts Committee (PPAC)
options.C: The Chief Minister's inspection team alone

correctAnswerText: The Provincial Public Accounts Committee (PPAC)
explanation: Each Provincial Assembly has its own standing Public Accounts Committee to examine provincial department audits.
subCategory: Audit Planning, Conduct, Reporting & PAC Role

questionText: An 'Audit Working Paper' in public sector auditing must document:

options.A: Audit objective, scope, methodology, evidence gathered, criteria used, and conclusions reached
options.B: Personal travel itinerary of the auditor
options.C: Private political opinions of the audit team

correctAnswerText: Audit objective, scope, methodology, evidence gathered, criteria used, and conclusions reached
explanation: Working papers provide a clear audit trail proving that the audit was conducted in compliance with INTOSAI/DAGP standards.
subCategory: Audit Planning, Conduct, Reporting & PAC Role

questionText: Under DAGP standards, working papers must be retained for at least:

options.A: 10 years (or until final PAC disposal of the relevant paras)

correctAnswerText: 10 years (or until final PAC disposal of the relevant paras)
explanation: Public sector audit files must be preserved until the audit para is conclusively settled by the PAC or under statutory archiving rules.
subCategory: Audit Planning, Conduct, Reporting & PAC Role

questionText: What is an 'Unqualified (Clean) Audit Report' issued by the AGP on government financial statements?

options.A: A report stating that financial statements present fairly, in all material respects, the budget execution and financial transactions
options.B: A report stating the government has no money left
options.C: A report without the auditor's signature
options.D: A report stating all ministers are honest

correctAnswerText: A report stating that financial statements present fairly, in all material respects, the budget execution and financial transactions
explanation: An unqualified report certifies that the financial statements comply with the prescribed accounting model without material reservation.
subCategory: Audit Planning, Conduct, Reporting & PAC Role

questionText: The document containing the audited comparison between Parliament's budget authorizations and actual departmental expenditures is the:

options.A: Appropriation Accounts

correctAnswerText: Appropriation Accounts
explanation: Appropriation Accounts contrast authorized grants against actual disbursements, detailing excess expenditures or surrendered savings.
subCategory: Audit Planning, Conduct, Reporting & PAC Role

questionText: The document containing the summary of cash transactions, public debt, receipts, and revenue collections of the Federation is the:

options.A: Finance Accounts

correctAnswerText: Finance Accounts
explanation: Finance Accounts present the annual accounts of government receipts, disbursements, public debt, and balances.
subCategory: Audit Planning, Conduct, Reporting & PAC Role

questionText: The primary forum for holding public hearings on the AGP's audit reports is:

options.A: Public Accounts Committee hearings open to media and official recording

correctAnswerText: Public Accounts Committee hearings open to media and official recording
explanation: PAC hearings provide public, recorded legislative review where the executive must publicly explain audit discrepancies.
subCategory: Audit Planning, Conduct, Reporting & PAC Role

questionText: If a Principal Accounting Officer (PAO) willfully disobeys PAC directives or refuses to appear before PAC, PAC can:

options.A: Issue warrants for non-attendance through the Speaker of the National Assembly

correctAnswerText: Issue warrants for non-attendance through the Speaker of the National Assembly
explanation: Under parliamentary privilege rules, the PAC Chairman/Speaker may issue bailable/non-bailable warrants to compel the attendance of errant officials.
subCategory: Audit Planning, Conduct, Reporting & PAC Role

questionText: In performance audit reporting, recommendations should be:

options.A: Constructive, practical, cost-effective, and addressing root causes (SMART)
options.D: Focused only on punishing junior clerks

correctAnswerText: Constructive, practical, cost-effective, and addressing root causes (SMART)
explanation: ISSAI 300 mandates that performance audit recommendations be constructive, realistic, cost-effective, and targeted at systemic improvements.
subCategory: Audit Planning, Conduct, Reporting & PAC Role

questionText: The concept of 'Value for Money' (VFM) in public sector reporting encapsulates:

options.A: Economy, Efficiency, and Effectiveness (the 3Es)
options.B: Maximum tax extraction from poor citizens
options.D: Spending the budget in the final week of June

correctAnswerText: Economy, Efficiency, and Effectiveness (the 3Es)
explanation: VFM auditing evaluates optimal stewardship: minimizing cost (economy), maximizing ratio of outputs to inputs (efficiency), and hitting goals (effectiveness).
subCategory: Audit Planning, Conduct, Reporting & PAC Role

questionText: A 'Special Audit Report' produced by the AGP relates to:

options.A: An in-depth investigation into a specific high-value mega-project, disaster relief, or public crisis
options.C: Daily fuel consumption of a single jeep
options.D: Annual tax assessment of a private firm

correctAnswerText: An in-depth investigation into a specific high-value mega-project, disaster relief, or public crisis
explanation: Special audit reports delve into major national programs (e.g. COVID relief funds, LNG terminals, motorway construction) requiring dedicated evaluation.
subCategory: Audit Planning, Conduct, Reporting & PAC Role

questionText: What is the final stage of the legislative accountability cycle in Pakistan?

options.A: The PAC presents its consolidated report and recommendations to the National Assembly for formal adoption

correctAnswerText: The PAC presents its consolidated report and recommendations to the National Assembly for formal adoption
explanation: The PAC compiles its findings and recommendations into reports laid before the full National Assembly for discussion and adoption.
subCategory: Audit Planning, Conduct, Reporting & PAC Role

questionText: In the audit reporting hierarchy, who signs the formal Audit Reports submitted to the President of Pakistan?

options.A: The Auditor General of Pakistan personally
options.D: The Director General of Audit only

correctAnswerText: The Auditor General of Pakistan personally
explanation: The formal constitutional reports submitted to the President under Article 171 bear the official signature of the Auditor General of Pakistan.
subCategory: Audit Planning, Conduct, Reporting & PAC Role

questionText: A 'System Audit' conducted by DAGP assesses:

options.A: The design and operation of internal control mechanisms, IT databases, and computerized accounting systems
options.B: The physical weight of desktop computers
options.C: The speed of internet connections in audit offices

correctAnswerText: The design and operation of internal control mechanisms, IT databases, and computerized accounting systems
explanation: System audits evaluate institutional processes, internal checks, data integrity, and internal control structures.
subCategory: Audit Planning, Conduct, Reporting & PAC Role

questionText: The term 'Sub-Committee of PAC' refers to:

options.A: A smaller specialized group of PAC members assigned to examine voluminous backlogs or specific ministry accounts

correctAnswerText: A smaller specialized group of PAC members assigned to examine voluminous backlogs or specific ministry accounts
explanation: PAC creates sub-committees to expedite scrutiny of extensive audit backlogs or focused departmental portfolios.
subCategory: Audit Planning, Conduct, Reporting & PAC Role

questionText: Audit paras that involve systemic policy flaws rather than individual corruption are termed:

options.A: Systemic / Policy-level Audit Observations

correctAnswerText: Systemic / Policy-level Audit Observations
explanation: Systemic observations identify structural loopholes in laws, rules, or automated systems that permit recurring inefficiencies or losses.
subCategory: Audit Planning, Conduct, Reporting & PAC Role

questionText: When the PAC 'settles' an audit para, it means:

options.A: The PAC is satisfied that compliance has been verified, recoveries completed, or appropriate disciplinary action taken by the ministry
options.B: The ministry paid a bribe to the committee

correctAnswerText: The PAC is satisfied that compliance has been verified, recoveries completed, or appropriate disciplinary action taken by the ministry
explanation: Settlement of a para occurs when the PAC formally concludes that the auditee has fulfilled all audit requirements and verified remedial action.
subCategory: Audit Planning, Conduct, Reporting & PAC Role

questionText: An 'Interim Audit Report' may be issued when:

options.A: Immediate corrective intervention by government is critical prior to completion of the full annual audit cycle
options.B: The auditor wants an early vacation

correctAnswerText: Immediate corrective intervention by government is critical prior to completion of the full annual audit cycle
explanation: Urgent findings of ongoing severe losses or structural collapse are highlighted early via interim reports to prompt swift remediation.
subCategory: Audit Planning, Conduct, Reporting & PAC Role

questionText: Who is responsible for taking departmental disciplinary action against delinquent officials named in audit reports?

options.A: The Principal Accounting Officer (PAO) and administrative executive authorities

correctAnswerText: The Principal Accounting Officer (PAO) and administrative executive authorities
explanation: Administrative disciplinary proceedings under Civil Servants (E&D) Rules are the executive responsibility of the PAO/Ministry.
subCategory: Audit Planning, Conduct, Reporting & PAC Role

questionText: The DAGP Audit Management Information System (AMIS) is:

options.A: An automated digital platform used to plan, track, execute, and monitor audits and audit paras across Pakistan
options.C: A tax filing portal for citizens

correctAnswerText: An automated digital platform used to plan, track, execute, and monitor audits and audit paras across Pakistan
explanation: AMIS is DAGP's specialized IT system automating audit planning, field observations, draft paras, and tracking PAC settlements.
subCategory: Audit Planning, Conduct, Reporting & PAC Role

questionText: Audit findings that highlight non-deduction of Income Tax or Sales Tax by government disbursing officers relate to:

options.A: Statutory tax withholding compliance audit

correctAnswerText: Statutory tax withholding compliance audit
explanation: Auditing withholding tax deductions (WHT) on government procurement payments ensures compliance with the Income Tax Ordinance and Sales Tax Act.
subCategory: Audit Planning, Conduct, Reporting & PAC Role

questionText: The overarching objective of the Public Accounts Committee and Supreme Audit Institution collaboration is to:

options.A: Ensure public resources are utilized with integrity, economy, efficiency, and constitutional accountability to the citizens
options.B: Maximize the salaries of members of Parliament

correctAnswerText: Ensure public resources are utilized with integrity, economy, efficiency, and constitutional accountability to the citizens
explanation: The supreme aim of SAI audit and PAC oversight is upholding transparency, public trust, and democratic accountability in public finance.
subCategory: Audit Planning, Conduct, Reporting & PAC Role

questionText: What is the fundamental difference between Cash Basis and Accrual Basis of accounting?

options.A: Cash basis records transactions only when cash is received or paid; Accrual basis recognizes revenues when earned and expenses when incurred, regardless of cash flow
options.B: Cash basis is only used by banks; Accrual basis is used by street vendors
options.C: Cash basis requires computers; Accrual basis is done manually

correctAnswerText: Cash basis records transactions only when cash is received or paid; Accrual basis recognizes revenues when earned and expenses when incurred, regardless of cash flow
explanation: Cash accounting tracks physical cash flows; accrual accounting matches revenues and expenses to the period in which economic events occur.

questionText: Traditional government accounting in Pakistan historically operated on which basis?

options.A: Strict Accrual Basis

correctAnswerText: Cash Basis of Accounting
explanation: Traditional public sector accounting in Pakistan recorded receipts and payments when cash crossed treasury counters.

questionText: What does IPSAS stand for?

options.A: International Public Sector Accounting Standards
options.D: Intergovernmental Protocol for State Audit Schemes

correctAnswerText: International Public Sector Accounting Standards
explanation: IPSAS are high-quality accounting standards issued by the IPSASB for use by public sector entities worldwide.

questionText: The International Public Sector Accounting Standards Board (IPSASB) operates under the auspices of:

options.A: International Federation of Accountants (IFAC)

correctAnswerText: International Federation of Accountants (IFAC)
explanation: The IPSASB is an independent standard-setting board supported by the International Federation of Accountants (IFAC).

questionText: The primary purpose of developing IPSAS is to:

options.A: Improve the quality, transparency, and comparability of public sector financial reporting globally

correctAnswerText: Improve the quality, transparency, and comparability of public sector financial reporting globally
explanation: IPSAS aims to enhance financial reporting by public sector entities, leading to better-informed public resource allocation decisions.

questionText: How many parts does the 'Cash Basis IPSAS' standard consist of?

options.A: Part 1 (Mandatory Requirements) and Part 2 (Encouraged Additional Disclosures)

correctAnswerText: Part 1 (Mandatory Requirements) and Part 2 (Encouraged Additional Disclosures)
explanation: The Cash Basis IPSAS comprises Part 1 (mandatory rules for statement of cash receipts and payments) and Part 2 (encouraged disclosures like liabilities/assets).

questionText: Under Cash Basis IPSAS, the primary financial statement required is the:

options.A: Statement of Cash Receipts and Payments

correctAnswerText: Statement of Cash Receipts and Payments
explanation: The cornerstone mandatory statement under Cash Basis IPSAS is the Statement of Cash Receipts and Payments.

questionText: Under Accrual Basis IPSAS, a complete set of financial statements includes:

options.A: Statement of Financial Position, Statement of Financial Performance, Statement of Changes in Net Assets/Equity, Cash Flow Statement, and Notes
options.D: Only the list of government vehicles

correctAnswerText: Statement of Financial Position, Statement of Financial Performance, Statement of Changes in Net Assets/Equity, Cash Flow Statement, and Notes
explanation: IPSAS 1 mandates: Statement of Financial Position, Financial Performance, Changes in Net Assets/Equity, Cash Flow Statement, and Accounting Policies/Notes.

questionText: In Accrual Basis IPSAS, the equivalent term for 'Balance Sheet' is:

options.A: Statement of Financial Position

correctAnswerText: Statement of Financial Position
explanation: IPSAS 1 designates the balance sheet as the 'Statement of Financial Position'.

questionText: In Accrual Basis IPSAS, the equivalent term for 'Income Statement' or 'Profit and Loss Account' is:

options.A: Statement of Financial Performance

correctAnswerText: Statement of Financial Performance
explanation: IPSAS 1 titles the operating performance statement the 'Statement of Financial Performance'.

questionText: Which IPSAS standard governs the 'Presentation of Financial Statements'?

options.A: IPSAS 1

correctAnswerText: IPSAS 1
explanation: IPSAS 1 sets out overall requirements for the presentation of financial statements under the accrual basis.

questionText: Which IPSAS standard deals with 'Cash Flow Statements' under the accrual framework?

options.A: IPSAS 2

correctAnswerText: IPSAS 2
explanation: IPSAS 2 outlines requirements for preparing and presenting the Cash Flow Statement.

questionText: Which IPSAS deals with 'Accounting Policies, Changes in Accounting Estimates and Errors'?

options.A: IPSAS 3

correctAnswerText: IPSAS 3
explanation: IPSAS 3 prescribes criteria for selecting and changing accounting policies, treatment of changes in estimates, and correction of errors.

questionText: Which IPSAS addresses 'Property, Plant and Equipment' (PPE) in the public sector?

options.A: IPSAS 17

correctAnswerText: IPSAS 17
explanation: IPSAS 17 establishes the accounting treatment for non-current physical assets, including recognition, measurement, and depreciation.

questionText: Under IPSAS 17, how are heritage assets (e.g. historical monuments, archaeological sites) treated?

options.A: An entity is not required to recognize heritage assets, but if recognized, disclosure and measurement standards apply
options.B: Heritage assets must be sold immediately
options.C: Heritage assets must be converted to cash within 30 days
options.D: Heritage assets are completely forbidden from government books

correctAnswerText: An entity is not required to recognize heritage assets, but if recognized, disclosure and measurement standards apply
explanation: IPSAS 17 does not mandate recognition of heritage assets due to valuation difficulties, but encourages disclosure if recognized.

questionText: Which IPSAS governs 'Inventories' in public sector organizations?

options.A: IPSAS 12

correctAnswerText: IPSAS 12
explanation: IPSAS 12 outlines the valuation and accounting treatment of inventories (at lower of cost and current replacement cost / NRV).

questionText: Under IPSAS 12, inventories held for distribution at no charge or for a nominal charge are valued at:

options.A: Lower of Cost and Current Replacement Cost

correctAnswerText: Lower of Cost and Current Replacement Cost
explanation: Public sector entities distributing goods (e.g., vaccines, schoolbooks) for free measure inventory at the lower of cost and current replacement cost.

questionText: Which IPSAS governs 'Revenue from Exchange Transactions'?

options.A: IPSAS 9

correctAnswerText: IPSAS 9
explanation: IPSAS 9 deals with exchange transactions where goods/services are provided in return for approximately equal value (e.g., utility tariffs).

questionText: Which IPSAS governs 'Revenue from Non-Exchange Transactions (Taxes and Transfers)'?

options.A: IPSAS 23

correctAnswerText: IPSAS 23
explanation: IPSAS 23 is a cornerstone public sector standard regulating tax receipts, fines, grants, and transfers where no direct equal exchange is returned.

questionText: In a 'Non-Exchange Transaction' under IPSAS 23:

options.A: An entity receives value from another entity without directly giving approximately equal value in exchange
options.B: Commercial buyers purchase goods at market rates
options.C: The government barters equal volumes of petroleum

correctAnswerText: An entity receives value from another entity without directly giving approximately equal value in exchange
explanation: Taxation and government grants are non-exchange transactions because taxpayers do not receive a direct, equal quid pro quo.

questionText: Which IPSAS deals with 'Provisions, Contingent Liabilities and Contingent Assets'?

options.A: IPSAS 19

correctAnswerText: IPSAS 19
explanation: IPSAS 19 guides recognition and measurement of provisions and contingent items in public sector accounts.

questionText: Which IPSAS deals with 'Presentation of Budget Information in Financial Statements'?

options.A: IPSAS 24

correctAnswerText: IPSAS 24
explanation: IPSAS 24 requires a comparison of budget and actual amounts in financial statements for entities held publicly accountable for approved budgets.

questionText: Under IPSAS 24, public sector entities must present a comparison of:

options.A: Original budget, final revised budget, and actual expenditure amounts on the same basis as the budget

correctAnswerText: Original budget, final revised budget, and actual expenditure amounts on the same basis as the budget
explanation: IPSAS 24 mandates reconciliation and comparison between approved budget figures and actual accounting outcomes.

questionText: What is the 'New Accounting Model' (NAM) in Pakistan?

options.A: A modernized, computerized accounting system introduced under the PIFRA project based on modified cash/accrual concepts and a comprehensive Chart of Accounts
options.B: A tax collection manual of provincial excise
options.C: A private banking software developed in London

correctAnswerText: A modernized, computerized accounting system introduced under the PIFRA project based on modified cash/accrual concepts and a comprehensive Chart of Accounts
explanation: NAM was developed under PIFRA (Project to Improve Financial Reporting and Auditing) to modernize Pakistan's government financial reporting.

questionText: Under NAM, the Chart of Accounts (COA) is structured around how many distinct elements?

options.A: Five elements: Entity, Function, Object, Fund, and Project

correctAnswerText: Five elements: Entity, Function, Object, Fund, and Project
explanation: NAM COA uses five dimensions: Entity (who), Function (why), Object (what), Fund (source of finance), and Project (specific plan).

questionText: In the NAM Chart of Accounts, the 'Object Element' classifies:

options.A: The nature of expenditure or receipt (e.g., A01 Salaries, A03 Operating Expenses, A09 Physical Assets)
options.B: The name of the administrative ministry

correctAnswerText: The nature of expenditure or receipt (e.g., A01 Salaries, A03 Operating Expenses, A09 Physical Assets)
explanation: The Object code classifies transactions into economic categories: personnel, operating costs, transfers, capital assets, etc.

questionText: In the NAM Chart of Accounts, the 'Function Element' classifies:

options.A: The social, economic, or administrative purpose of expenditure (e.g., 01 General Public Services, 02 Defense, 09 Education)

correctAnswerText: The social, economic, or administrative purpose of expenditure (e.g., 01 General Public Services, 02 Defense, 09 Education)
explanation: The Function code categorizes expenditure according to the UN Classification of Functions of Government (COFOG).

questionText: In the NAM Chart of Accounts, the 'Entity Element' identifies:

options.A: The specific organizational unit, ministry, department, or cost center incurring the transaction

correctAnswerText: The specific organizational unit, ministry, department, or cost center incurring the transaction
explanation: Entity defines organizational ownership: Ministry -> Division -> Department -> Field Office/Drawing & Disbursing Officer (DDO).

questionText: The Controller General of Accounts (CGA) in Pakistan is responsible for:

options.A: Preparing and maintaining the accounts of the Federation and Provinces and managing accounting operations

correctAnswerText: Preparing and maintaining the accounts of the Federation and Provinces and managing accounting operations
explanation: Under Ordinance XXIV of 2001, the CGA is responsible for preparing federal/provincial financial accounts and supervising treasury offices.

questionText: Under the separation of accounting and auditing in 2001, the CGA functions under the administrative control of:

options.A: The Ministry of Finance

correctAnswerText: The Ministry of Finance
explanation: The CGA is an attached department of the Federal Ministry of Finance, whereas the AGP is an independent constitutional watchdog.

questionText: Financial Statements of the Federal Government prepared by the CGA are audited by:

options.A: The Auditor General of Pakistan

correctAnswerText: The Auditor General of Pakistan
explanation: The AGP conducts the independent Financial Attest Audit of the annual financial statements prepared by the CGA.

questionText: The Project to Improve Financial Reporting and Auditing (PIFRA) implemented which ERP software across Pakistan's audit and accounts offices?

options.A: SAP (Systems, Applications, and Products)

correctAnswerText: SAP (Systems, Applications, and Products)
explanation: PIFRA implemented SAP ERP across all CGA accounting formations (AGPR, Provincial AGs, District Accounts Offices) and DAGP.

questionText: AGPR stands for:

options.A: Accountant General Pakistan Revenues

correctAnswerText: Accountant General Pakistan Revenues
explanation: AGPR is the principal federal accounting office responsible for centralized payment and accounting of the Federal Government.

questionText: In provincial capitals, federal government payments and accounting are handled by:

options.A: Sub-offices of AGPR (e.g., AGPR Sub-office Lahore, Karachi, Peshawar, Quetta)

correctAnswerText: Sub-offices of AGPR (e.g., AGPR Sub-office Lahore, Karachi, Peshawar, Quetta)
explanation: AGPR maintains sub-offices in provincial capitals to process federal civilian claims outside Islamabad.

questionText: Provincial government accounts in Punjab, Sindh, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, and Balochistan are headed by:

options.A: Accountant General (AG) of the respective province

correctAnswerText: Accountant General (AG) of the respective province
explanation: Each province has an Accountant General (e.g., AG Punjab, AG Sindh) heading provincial accounting operations under CGA.

questionText: At the district level in Pakistan, government payments and revenue accounts are processed through:

options.A: District Accounts Offices (DAOs)

correctAnswerText: District Accounts Offices (DAOs)
explanation: DAOs process civil claims, authorize bills, and maintain accounting ledgers for provincial formations at the district level.

questionText: A Drawing and Disbursing Officer (DDO) is:

options.A: An authorized government official empowered to draw funds against budget allocations and incur sanctioned disbursements

correctAnswerText: An authorized government official empowered to draw funds against budget allocations and incur sanctioned disbursements
explanation: A DDO is a departmental officer formally designated to draw public money from treasuries and disburse payments.

questionText: The 'Pre-Audit' system in government accounting entails:

options.A: Scrutiny and verification of bills/claims by the accounting office (AGPR/DAO) BEFORE payment is authorized and cheques issued
options.C: Auditing the client before they are born
options.D: Checking bills after money is permanently lost

correctAnswerText: Scrutiny and verification of bills/claims by the accounting office (AGPR/DAO) BEFORE payment is authorized and cheques issued
explanation: Pre-audit is an internal accounting control where claims are verified for legality, sanction, budget, and vouchers prior to cheque disbursement.

questionText: The 'Post-Audit' system refers to:

options.A: Independent audit conducted by the Auditor General AFTER transactions have taken place and payments disbursed
options.B: Audit performed before budget is drafted
options.C: Checking vouchers before signing a contract

correctAnswerText: Independent audit conducted by the Auditor General AFTER transactions have taken place and payments disbursed
explanation: Post-audit is the retrospective, independent examination of completed transactions by external auditors (DAGP).

questionText: Under IPSAS 28, 30, and 32, public sector 'Service Concession Arrangements' (Public-Private Partnerships - PPP) address:

options.A: Accounting treatment of infrastructure built and operated by private operators for public service delivery

correctAnswerText: Accounting treatment of infrastructure built and operated by private operators for public service delivery
explanation: IPSAS 32 governs accounting for grantor (government) assets and liabilities in PPP service concession arrangements.

questionText: Under Accrual Basis IPSAS, Depreciation on state infrastructure assets (such as highways and bridges):

options.A: Must be recognized systematically over their estimated useful operational lives
options.D: Is expensed only when the bridge collapses

correctAnswerText: Must be recognized systematically over their estimated useful operational lives
explanation: Under IPSAS 17, infrastructure assets are capitalized and depreciated systematically over their useful lives.

questionText: The concept of 'Commitment Accounting' in public financial management tracks:

options.A: Budget reservations made when purchase orders or contracts are signed, before actual delivery or invoice receipt

correctAnswerText: Budget reservations made when purchase orders or contracts are signed, before actual delivery or invoice receipt
explanation: Commitment accounting reserves budget funds upon issuing legal procurement orders, preventing over-commitment of approved allocations.

questionText: Modified Cash Basis of accounting differs from Pure Cash Basis because:

options.A: It keeps books open for a specified period (e.g., supplementary period) after year-end to record payments for past liabilities
options.C: It values inventory at current stock market prices
options.D: It reports in foreign currency only

correctAnswerText: It keeps books open for a specified period (e.g., supplementary period) after year-end to record payments for past liabilities
explanation: Modified cash accounting recognizes transactions shortly after the fiscal year close that relate to goods/services received within the year.

questionText: Under IPSAS, non-current assets held for sale are governed by:

options.A: IPSAS standards aligned with IFRS 5

correctAnswerText: IPSAS standards aligned with IFRS 5
explanation: IPSASB aligns standards with IFRSs where appropriate, measuring assets held for sale at lower of carrying amount and fair value less costs to sell.

questionText: Under IPSAS 39 (Employee Benefits), public sector defined-benefit pensions are measured using:

options.A: Actuarial valuation using the Projected Unit Credit Method
options.C: The amount of cash in the treasury on June 30
options.D: Zero liability until the employee reaches age 100

correctAnswerText: Actuarial valuation using the Projected Unit Credit Method
explanation: IPSAS 39 mandates actuarial measurement (Projected Unit Credit Method) to recognize defined-benefit pension obligations on the balance sheet.

questionText: The main benefit of transitioning from Cash Basis to Accrual Basis IPSAS for governments is:

options.A: Comprehensive visibility of all state assets, liabilities, pension obligations, and true financial sustainability
options.B: Immediate elimination of all public taxes
options.C: Allowing governments to borrow without limits
options.D: Ending all need for internal controls

correctAnswerText: Comprehensive visibility of all state assets, liabilities, pension obligations, and true financial sustainability
explanation: Accrual IPSAS provides full transparency of public wealth, true operating costs, future commitments, and long-term fiscal solvency.

questionText: In the Federal Government of Pakistan, the fiscal year runs from:

options.A: 1st July to 30th June of the following calendar year

correctAnswerText: 1st July to 30th June of the following calendar year
explanation: Pakistan's financial year spans 1st July through 30th June.

questionText: What is an 'Assigned Account' or 'Revolving Fund Account' in government accounting?

options.A: A designated bank account operated by a project director with special withdrawal limits to expedite project execution
options.B: A personal savings account of the minister
options.D: An account that cannot be audited

correctAnswerText: A designated bank account operated by a project director with special withdrawal limits to expedite project execution
explanation: Assigned accounts are specialized bank accounts funded through budgetary releases to facilitate project disbursements under prescribed rules.

questionText: The SAP system implemented under PIFRA utilizes which transaction code interface to process accounting vouchers in Pakistan?

options.A: Core SAP R/3 financial modules (FI/CO/FM)

correctAnswerText: Core SAP R/3 financial modules (FI/CO/FM)
explanation: PIFRA uses SAP Financial Accounting (FI), Funds Management (FM), and Controlling (CO) modules for public financial data.

questionText: In public sector financial statements under IPSAS, 'Net Assets / Equity' represents:

options.A: The residual interest in the assets of the entity after deducting all its liabilities
options.B: The total paper money printed by the central bank
options.C: The market price of all private buildings
options.D: Total foreign debt divided by population

correctAnswerText: The residual interest in the assets of the entity after deducting all its liabilities
explanation: In IPSAS 1, Net Assets/Equity = Total Assets minus Total Liabilities.

questionText: The Public Finance Management (PFM) Act, 2019 was enacted by the Parliament of Pakistan to:

options.A: Strengthen management of public finances, institutionalize fiscal discipline, and establish sound financial governance
options.D: Eliminate the office of the Auditor General

correctAnswerText: Strengthen management of public finances, institutionalize fiscal discipline, and establish sound financial governance
explanation: The PFM Act 2019 was enacted to institutionalize fiscal discipline, improve budget formulation, enhance cash management, and ensure fiscal transparency.
subCategory: Public Finance Management Act, 2019 & PPRA Rules

questionText: Under Section 2(m) of the PFM Act 2019, who is designated as the 'Principal Accounting Officer' (PAO) for a Ministry or Division?

options.A: The Secretary of the administrative Ministry or Division

correctAnswerText: The Secretary of the administrative Ministry or Division
explanation: The Secretary of the Ministry or Division is designated as the PAO responsible for financial and budgetary management.
subCategory: Public Finance Management Act, 2019 & PPRA Rules

questionText: Under the PFM Act 2019, the Principal Accounting Officer is assisted in financial planning and internal control by the:

options.A: Chief Finance and Accounts Officer (CFAO)

correctAnswerText: Chief Finance and Accounts Officer (CFAO)
explanation: Under PFM Act reforms, the PAO is assisted by a specialized Chief Finance and Accounts Officer (CFAO) stationed within the ministry.
subCategory: Public Finance Management Act, 2019 & PPRA Rules

questionText: Under the PFM Act 2019, what is the 'Treasury Single Account' (TSA)?

options.A: A unified structure of government bank accounts through which the government consolidates its cash balances and manages cash resources centrally
options.B: A single ATM card held by the Finance Minister
options.C: A bank account for paying traffic fines
options.D: A personal checking account in a commercial bank

correctAnswerText: A unified structure of government bank accounts through which the government consolidates its cash balances and manages cash resources centrally
explanation: The TSA consolidates all public cash balances under the State Bank of Pakistan, eliminating idle commercial bank deposits.
subCategory: Public Finance Management Act, 2019 & PPRA Rules

questionText: Under Section 3 of the PFM Act 2019, the Federal Government must prepare and submit to the Cabinet a multi-year document known as:

options.A: Budget Strategy Paper (BSP)

correctAnswerText: Budget Strategy Paper (BSP)
explanation: The Federal Government prepares a rolling 3-year Budget Strategy Paper articulating medium-term fiscal objectives, revenues, and expenditures.
subCategory: Public Finance Management Act, 2019 & PPRA Rules

questionText: By which date must the Federal Government submit the Budget Strategy Paper to the Standing Committees of Parliament under the PFM Act 2019?

options.A: By 15th April each year

correctAnswerText: By 15th April each year
explanation: Section 3 mandates sharing the Budget Strategy Paper with Parliamentary standing committees by mid-April for legislative consultation.
subCategory: Public Finance Management Act, 2019 & PPRA Rules

questionText: Under Section 11 of the PFM Act 2019, all anticipated budget savings must be surrendered by the PAO to the Finance Division by:

options.A: 31st May of each fiscal year

correctAnswerText: 31st May of each fiscal year
explanation: The PFM Act stipulates that unspent funds that cannot be utilized must be formally surrendered by 31st May to prevent year-end rush of expenditure.
subCategory: Public Finance Management Act, 2019 & PPRA Rules

questionText: Under the Constitution and PFM rules, what happens to unspent budgetary appropriations at the close of the financial year on 30th June?

options.A: They automatically lapse to the Consolidated Fund
